knowledge_gaps: The proposed item-pair mean gap cannot distinguish different elapsed times for the same transition. It tests a transition-conditioned temporal proxy, so claims about adapting to each user's changing intent need stronger justification.

The gate offset beta*tanh(g) is not bounded during training because beta is unconstrained. Also, tanh(log1p(days)) rapidly saturates, potentially obscuring differences between moderately long and very long gaps.
A missing pair and a genuinely zero elapsed gap receive the same feature. Pair coverage, observation counts, timestamp units, invalid-interval aggregation, and sparse lookup storage are unspecified.
The comparison lacks controls that distinguish timestamp information from additional gate capacity or item-pair identity. A constant-offset control and a shuffled-gap control would help.

Replacing a fused GRU with a Python recurrence may substantially increase GPU time. Multilayer state masking, dropout behavior, parameter mapping, gradient equivalence at beta=0, and checkpoint–predictor parity need explicit implementation details.

Potential 7/10 and difficulty 5/10 appear optimistic without proxy coverage measurements or runtime estimates. The report also changes direction from BPR-max without evidence that the temporal proxy is a stronger next experiment.
No affordable comparison schedule or uncertainty assessment is specified. Small selected HR@10 gains may reflect validation selection noise; training diagnostics cannot establish temporal usefulness.
